newsitem.title: FRANCE: Minister seeks "transparent" sale of Thomson-CSF.
newsitem.headline: Minister seeks "transparent" sale of Thomson-CSF.

text.p: French Industry Minister Franck Borotra said in a newspaper interview he wanted the procedure for privatising electronics group Thomson CSF to "be transparent."

In an interview with Les Echos due to be published Friday, Borotra said the decision on Thomson's future should pave the way for the company to be at the heart of the European electronics industry and play a world role.
The government's decision on the sale is expected sometime before the end of February.
"If the state opts for an industrial solution, it could seek to integrate as fast as possible all of the electronic defence companies but that's not easy to do," he said.
"It could also seek to strengthen certain Thomson-CSF activities by alliances...," he said.
He said the decision was crucial because it would determine "who will be the architect of the industrial restructuring of the defence electronics industry."
He said while intense competition made it desirable to build a strong defence electronics industry uniting all players, that would not be easy to achieve.

Thomson-CSF is being sold following a failed attempt to privatise its parent Thomson SA. The government suspended Thomson SA's proposed sale to Lagardere after it ran into fierce public opposition and did not receive approval from the independent Privatisation Commission.
